The shell invocation means any shell metacharacters or environment variable expansion could be exploited.

findings.description: Insecure cookie handling with default secure flag set to False in create_cookie function
findings.code_snippet:
def create_cookie(name, value, **kwargs):
    """Make a cookie from underspecified parameters.

    By default, the pair of `name` and `value` will be set for the domain ''
    and sent on every request (this is sometimes called a "supercookie").
    """
    result = {
        "version": 0,
        "name": name,
        "value": value,
        "port": None,
        "domain": "",
        "path": "/",
        "secure": False,
        "expires": None,
        "discard": True,
        "comment": None,
        "comment_url": None,
        "rest": {"HttpOnly": None},
        "rfc2109": False,
    }

    badargs = set(kwargs) - set(result)
    if badargs:
        raise TypeError(
            f"create_cookie() got unexpected keyword arguments: {list(badargs)}"
        )

    result.update(kwargs)
    result["port_specified"] = bool(result["port"])
    result["domain_specified"] = bool(result["domain"])
    result["domain_initial_dot"] = result["domain"].startswith(".")
    result["path_specified"] = bool(result["path"])

    return cookielib.Cookie(**result)
findings.reasoning: The create_cookie function defaults the 'secure' flag to False (line 468). This means any cookie created without explicitly passing secure=True will be transmitted over both HTTP and HTTPS connections. This is a security vulnerability because sensitive cookies should only be transmitted over HTTPS. The function is called in multiple places (lines 221, 537) without enforcing the secure flag, allowing insecure cookies to be created by default.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: When create_cookie is called at line 221 (in RequestsCookieJar.set) or line 537 (in extract_cookies_to_jar), if the caller doesn't explicitly pass secure=True, the cookie will be created with secure=False, allowing transmission over insecure HTTP connections.
evidence.notes: The vulnerability affects cookie security across the requests library. Cookies created through the RequestsCookieJar.set method or extract_cookies_to_jar function without explicit secure flag will default to insecure transmission. This is particularly dangerous for authentication tokens and session cookies.

Since create_cookie() defaults to secure=False (line 468), cookies created through this call will be transmitted over both HTTP and HTTPS, exposing sensitive session data to man-in-the-middle attacks. This is a direct call to create_cookie without any secure flag parameter, relying on the insecure default.

evidence.code_context: In requests/cookies.py, the extract_code_snippet shows that at line 537, create_cookie is called with only name and value parameters: cookiejar.set_cookie(create_cookie(name, cookie_dict[name])). The create_cookie function definition at line 455-489 shows that the default value for 'secure' is hardcoded to False at line 468.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: The cookie_dict parameter comes from external input (function parameter), and cookies are created without enforcing secure flags. The secure flag defaults to False, meaning cookies will be sent over insecure HTTP connections.
evidence.notes: This is part of the extract_cookies_to_jar function which processes cookie dictionaries. Without explicit secure flag enforcement, all cookies created this way are vulnerable to interception over HTTP.
